messages:
maria: Heads-up — Platform plans to change the client-side debounce for routing hints and to rename the routing header from `X-Route` -> `X-PathHint`. This affects quota attribution in the console. Need quick alignment on SDK behavior + rollout windows.

Tom: Oof, header rename = classic break. Are we doing a hard cut or supporting both?

maria: We want a 2-week canary where servers accept both headers and prefer `X-PathHint`, then a 30d dual-accept shim before deprecation. But debounce change will change sampling cadence and could affect burst quotas on tenant dashboards.

jess: For the SDKs (py/ts/go) we should auto-send both headers for the shim period. Small patch on client libs.

kevin: Agree on dual-send. But we need telemetry flags so console can know which header source was used for each request (old vs new) for attribution. Otherwise billing/alerts will be noisy.

maria: Good point. We'll add a `route_header_version` field to telemetry events: `v1` for X-Route, `v2` for X-PathHint. Console team can wire that into quota dashboards.

dan: SDK perf-wise dual-send is trivial. The bigger change is debounce semantics — reducing debounce from 50ms -> 10ms to improve tail latency. That increases request rate ~5-10% in alpha tests. Need to surface that to ops.

olivia: Can we gate debounce change behind a feature flag per-tenant? That would let us roll it gradually and measure quota burn impact.

maria: Yes — plan is feature-flagged rollout via console, default off for enterprise tenants. We'll flip for internal test orgs first.

Tom: For the Python SDK, will this be a patch (non-breaking) or new minor? If we dual-send by default I'd call it a patch, but users relying on exact headers might see duplicates.

jess: We'll implement a non-breaking patch: if user supplies a custom header we won't override; otherwise SDK populates `X-PathHint` and leaves `X-Route` for 30d. Add opt-out config param `disable_pathhint_shim=true` for strict users.

kevin: Console owners: can you add a telemetry column (route_header_version) and a burn-rate diff metric to compare pre/post debounce per-tenant? We should also expose an alert when quota spend increases > 15% after flip.

olivia: Yup, file a console ticket and I'll prioritize a dashboard tile for the canary orgs.

maria: Deploy plan: 1) update server to accept both and emit header-version telemetry (deploy-bot: canary to internal orgs), 2) release SDK patches (py/ts/go) with dual-send shim and opt-out param, 3) enable debounce flag in console for canary, 4) monitor quota burn/latency for 72h, 5) roll to wider audience.

deploy-bot: Started canary deployment to `internal-test` @maria (build 2026.03.21-canary #42). Logs: https://ci.redwood/9876

sre-oncall: Heads-up: set pager threshold to +25% quota burn for canary orgs while monitoring. I'll mute noisy alerts but keep high-severity.

Tom: Docs note: update SDK changelogs and migration guide. Also call out the opt-out flag and the 30d shim period.

jess: I'll draft the SDK release notes and a short migration snippet:
```
# python example
from redwood import Client
client = Client(..., disable_pathhint_shim=False)  # default: shim on
client.request(...)
```

maria: Thanks everyone. Action items: jess (SDK patches + release notes), olivia (console tile + ticket), kevin (telemetry schema), dan (monitor perf numbers), dan/sre-oncall (paging thresholds). We'll sync tomorrow 10am if canary shows odd signals. :thumbsup:

olivia: Filed CONSOLE-2146 for dashboard tile and alerted the console oncall.

maria: Closing loop for now — we'll keep updates in this thread.
